title: Immutable golden prompt snapshots + signer-based access and provenance
creator: Ava Park
description:
Problem: As model/config changes trigger automated regression checks, we need a deterministic, auditable source-of-truth for golden prompt sets and golden response datasets that can be used by the eval pipeline, by on-call, and by customers during audits. Current prompt bundle edits are mutable and lack strong provenance or a simple rollback workflow, causing unclear regression roots and accidental test drift.

Scope: Deliver immutable snapshot artifacts for golden prompt sets (prompt text, metadata, expected outputs/eval harness mappings), signer-based access controls (who can publish a snapshot), UI + CLI to create/inspect snapshots, automatic checksum provenance stored alongside the snapshot, and integration hooks so the eval runner can pin to a snapshot id. Also add a lightweight diff UI in Console and an API for programmatic rollback and opt-in gating of releases based on snapshot-linked regression results.

Out of scope: Full RBAC rewrite; long-term archival tiering (follow-up project).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Product: Console shows a 'Snapshot' view for each golden prompt bundle with: snapshot id, creator, signer, checksum, creation timestamp, and changelog
2) Security: Only users with 'golden-signer' permission can publish snapshots; publishing requires a 2-step confirm in Console and a cryptographic HMAC signature attached to the artifact
3) Evals integration: Eval runner can accept a snapshot id and will always fetch the exact blob (checksum verified) used to generate baselines
4) Rollback: Team leads can select any previous snapshot and mark it 'active' for gating; this triggers an automated re-eval run and creates a rollback PR in the eval-results store
5) CLI & API: 'ri snapshot create|list|diff|inspect' commands exist and match Console state
6) Audit trail: Every snapshot publish/update action emits an audit log entry (user, timestamp, snapshot id, signature) and is queryable for at least 90 days
7) Docs: Runbook for on-call that explains how to pin models to snapshots, how to trigger a snapshot re-eval, and how to rollback when regression is confirmed
updates: 2025-08-12 - Created ticket after post-mortem from false-positive regression where prompt edits were the root cause (linked incident notes in Drive)

2025-09-03 - Scoping review with Security: agreed on signer-based publish model using HMAC keyed per user-service account; Security requested KMS-backed keys for signing (see doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abcExample)

2025-10-01 - Engineering spike (ENG-7724) completed: validated object storage + checksum strategy; suggested storage layout: s3://ri-golden-snapshots/{bundle}/{snapshot-id}/{manifest.json, prompts.ndjson, signatures.sig}

2025-11-18 - PM/Design sync: Console snapshot UX wireframes approved; added lightweight diffs for text and numeric expectation changes (design mock: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/golden-snapshots)
2026-01-12 - Security review 1: requested HMAC rotation policy and signer-role audit; assigned to security for final sign-off
2026-02-03 - Integrations: Eval runner changes merged that allow 'snapshot_id' parameter and checksum verification (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/compare/PR-4321)
2026-02-24 - Console backend PR opened to add snapshot endpoints and audit log plumbing (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1178), awaiting code review
2026-03-02 - Design feedback: add 'reason' field required for publish and optional 'rollback rationale' when marking active snapshot
2026-03-10 - QA smoke pass on staging: CLI create/list/diff work; found mismatch for multi-line expected outputs in ndjson canonicalization—assigned to ENG for normalization fix (ENG-13301)
open_questions: 1) Should snapshots be immutable forever or allowed a short TTL/retire flow for housekeeping? (security prefers immutability; infra wants TTL)
2) Do we require cryptographic signatures per human user or allow service accounts with delegation for automated pipelines?
3) Which team owns snapshot retention costs after 12 months? (Options: Evals infra budget vs centralized infra)
next_steps: 1) Finish normalization fix for ndjson canonicalization (ENG-13301) - blocker for release
2) Security finalize HMAC rotation policy and KMS integration (Deliverable: policy doc)
3) QA full re-eval workflow using snapshot id pinned to a canary model rollout (test plan in Confluence)
4) Prepare 'how-to' docs and runbook for on-call and solution engineers
